case_title: MUHAMMAD RIAZ VS ALLAH DITTA & others
full_text:
2026 SCMR 812
[Supreme Court of Pakistan]
Present: Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah, Justice Athar Minallah

MUHAMMAD RIAZ --- Petitioner
Versus
ALLAH DITTA & others --- Respondents

Civil Petition No. 412 of 2025, decided on 15th January, 2026.

(a) Punjab Pre-emption Act (IX of 1991)---
---S. 13(1) & S. 14---Suit for pre-emption---Performance of Talb-i-Muwathibat---Plea of illness / physical inability---Pre-emptor failed to perform Talb-i-Muwathibat immediately upon gaining knowledge of sale, claiming sudden illness---Effect---Held, Section 13(1) of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991 mandates that Talb-i-Muwathibat must be performed immediately when the pre-emptor gets information of the sale. Illness of the pre-emptor does not suspend or extend the statutory requirement of immediate performance of Talb-i-Muwathibat. Section 14 of the Act expressly authorizes a pre-emptor to appoint an agent/attorney or representative to make Talbs on his behalf if he is personally incapacitated or ill. Failure to make Talb-i-Muwathibat either in person or through a designated agent under Section 14 results in the extinguishment of the right of pre-emption. Pre-emption suit is liable to be dismissed on this sole ground. Petition dismissed.

(b) Pre-emption---
---Talbs---Nature of right---Right of pre-emption is a feeble right and strict compliance with the statutory provisions governing Talbs under Section 13 of Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1991 is mandatory.

case_title: TARIQ MEHMOOD VS PROVINCE OF PUNJAB & others
full_text:
2026 SCMR 901
[Supreme Court of Pakistan]
Present: Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan, Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail

TARIQ MEHMOOD --- Petitioner
Versus
PROVINCE OF PUNJAB & others --- Respondents

Civil Appeal No. 89 of 2025, decided on 2nd February, 2026.

(a) Punjab Pre-emption Act (IX of 1991)---
---S. 13---Pre-emption suit---Strict compliance with Talb-i-Muwathibat and Talb-i-Ishhad---Pre-emptor omitted to specify exact time, place, and names of witnesses of Talb-i-Muwathibat in the plaint---Defense of sudden illness and hospital admission raised to justify non-performance of immediate Talb-i-Muwathibat---Held, illness or hospitalization of pre-emptor cannot condone delay in making Talb-i-Muwathibat. The law of pre-emption under Section 13 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act 1991 does not contemplate any concession or extension of time for making the first demand (Talb-i-Muwathibat). If the pre-emptor is ill, he must utilize an authorized agent under Section 14. Non-performance of Talb-i-Muwathibat immediately is fatal to the pre-emption suit. Appeal dismissed.
